# Appeal of Denial — Total Ankle Replacement (CPT 27702)

**Governing policy cited by the plan:** Clinical Appropriateness Guidelines: Small Joint Surgery (Carelon) — https://files.providernews.anthem.com/2519/PDF-Small-Joint-Surgery-2023-11-05.pdf

**Member:** Sawyer Foster
**Member ID:** W558551284
**Plan:** Anthem Blue Cross Blue Shield (Commercial/ACA), New Hampshire
**Denial date:** 2026-08-01
**Reference number:** POC-64107D6EF7-65599

---

Dear Anthem Blue Cross Blue Shield Appeals Department,

I am writing to appeal the denial of my prior authorization request for a total ankle replacement (CPT 27702), as stated in the notice dated 2026-08-01, reference number POC-64107D6EF7-65599. The stated reason for denial was that "the documentation submitted was incomplete and does not allow a determination of medical necessity." My surgeon, Dr. Okafor, has documented that this procedure is medically necessary, and I am asking the plan to reconsider based on the records described below and, where the record is incomplete, to tell me specifically what is still needed so it can be provided.

## The Plan's Own Criteria and My Records

The Small Joint Surgery guideline states:

> "ankle arthroplasty is considered medically necessary in skeletally mature patients when ALL of the following criteria are met:"

> "• Radiographic confirmation of advanced/end-stage arthritis of the tibiotalar joint • Significant pain and functional impairment due to arthritis of the ankle persist after at least 3 months of supervised conservative management • Documentation of adequate lower extremity vascular perfusion (e.g., strong, palpable pedal pulses) • Device is FDA approved Total ankle arthroplasty may also be indicated for revision of failed previous reconstructions where sufficient bone stock and soft tissue integrity are present."

Here is how my records relate to each of these four requirements:

**1. Radiographic confirmation of advanced/end-stage arthritis of the tibiotalar joint.**
Weight-bearing ankle radiographs taken on 2026-06-05 showed tibiotalar joint space obliteration with subchondral cysts. I believe this satisfies the radiographic requirement.

**2. Significant pain and functional impairment persisting after at least 3 months of supervised conservative management.**
The guideline defines this as follows:

> "For the purposes of this guideline, significant pain and functional impairment refer to pain rated ≥ 4 on the VAS scale and associated with difficulty performing at least 2 impacted daily activities, such as walking and wearing reasonable shoes."

My records document 18 months of progressive ankle pain unrelieved by rest, an antalgic gait limited to two blocks, and range of motion limited by pain on exam. I completed 18 supervised physical therapy visits over 14 weeks (2026-03-09 to 2026-06-15), took NSAIDs for 4 months with inadequate relief, and received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-16 that gave only 4 weeks of partial relief. This is well beyond the 3-month conservative management period the guideline requires. The guideline also states:

> "Conservative management offered by the provider or other health professionals for this condition(s) should include footwear modification and/or padding/accommodative devices (e.g., foot orthosis) AND at least one of the following complementary strategies to reduce inflammation, alleviate pain, and improve function:"

> "• Activity modification • Anti-inflammatory medications and analgesics • Corticosteroid injection(s) • Debridement of associated hyperkeratotic lesions, such as corns or calluses Documentation of compliance with a plan of therapy that includes elements from these areas is required where conservative management is appropriate."

My records document NSAID use and a corticosteroid injection, which satisfy the "at least one" complementary strategy requirement. I do not see documentation in my file regarding footwear modification or padding/accommodative devices. [Placeholder: documentation of footwear modification or accommodative device use, if applicable, or a note from Dr. Okafor explaining why this element was not applicable, per the guideline's statement that "If conservative management is not appropriate, the medical record must clearly document why such an approach is not reasonable."]

I also do not see a specific numeric VAS pain score in the summary I have. [Placeholder: documented VAS pain score from the clinical record]. My records do document one impacted daily activity (walking, limited to two blocks); I am not aware of documentation addressing a second activity such as shoe-wearing. [Placeholder: documentation of a second impacted daily activity, if available].

**3. Documentation of adequate lower extremity vascular perfusion.**
I do not see this specifically documented in the summary available to me. [Placeholder: vascular exam findings, e.g., pedal pulse documentation, from Dr. Okafor's chart].

**4. Device is FDA approved.**
[Placeholder: confirmation from Dr. Okafor's office of the specific device/implant to be used and its FDA-approval status].

## Why I Am Asking for Reconsideration

The guideline states that Anthem's review vendor "applies objective and evidence-based criteria, and takes individual circumstances and the local delivery system into account when determining the medical appropriateness of health care services," and that "these criteria are designed to guide both providers and reviewers to the most appropriate services based on a patient's unique circumstances." Based on the records above, two of the four listed criteria — radiographic confirmation and the duration/nature of conservative management — appear to be clearly documented in my file. The denial reason given was incomplete documentation, not a finding that my condition fails to meet medical necessity. I am asking the plan to identify precisely which elements are considered missing so that Dr. Okafor's office can supply them, and to reconsider this request once the record is complete.

## What I Am Requesting

1. That Anthem Blue Cross Blue Shield reverse the denial of CPT 27702 for total ankle replacement, or
2. That Anthem specify exactly which documentation elements are still needed so my surgeon's office can submit them promptly.

I understand this appeal must be received by 2027-01-28. I have been advised to send this appeal to the address printed on my denial letter, or to submit it online through anthem.com or the Sydney Health app, or by calling the number on the back of my insurance ID card.

Please contact me if any additional information is needed.

Sincerely,

________________________________
Sawyer Foster
